solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrive to take care of male with minimal energy

parts.note: c/o is the usual written abbreviation for care of on an envelope

indicators.note: minimal here means the least possible of the word energy, just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to look after a man who is running low on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minimal energy' gives only the first letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to reach a place or turn up, simple synonyms.

clue.text: Prisoners upset by past vice

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters of past vice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Inmates are troubled by the wrongdoing that landed them in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the prisoners' mood but signals rearranging PASTVICE.
explanation.definitionFit: People held in captivity or confinement are prisoners, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gather food for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is as heard by listeners, a sound-alike

parts.note: meat is a kind of food

explanation.surface: People assemble to eat, presented as a show for spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble or come together is a common sense of both verbs.

clue.text: Bishop, worn out, blustered

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
ragged clothes are worn out, threadbare

explanation.surface: An exhausted bishop ranted.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluster is to talk loudly and boastfully, so blustered matches boasted loudly.

clue.text: Discarded item of furniture outside pub

indicators.note: outside says the furniture word goes round the pub word

parts.note: a bed is an item of furniture
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An old piece of furniture has been thrown out and left on the pavement by a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal, not where the furniture was left.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something in the rubbish bin is throwing it away, a British informal sense.

clue.text: A concept a kid worked out, full of excitement

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters of a concept a kid are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A child came up with an idea that turned out to be thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or story packed with action and thrills is exciting throughout.

clue.text: Good morsels thrown out? That's stupid

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters of morsels are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Throwing away good bits of food is a daft thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' reads as discarded but signals a reshuffle; the question mark nods to the surface verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for someone lacking sense, so dim or foolish.

clue.text: Buck's other half receives pounds as handout

indicators.note: receives says the deer word takes in the money letter

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, and its female partner is a doe
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man's partner takes in money as a welfare payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a man or a dollar; it is the male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit, a handout of money.

clue.text: Mad religions, sadly causing dismay

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters of mad religions are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fanatical faiths are, regrettably, upsetting people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that saps morale is disheartening, so it causes dismay.

clue.text: Unusual pattern a ruler re-established

indicators.note: re-established means set up again in a new form, so the letters of pattern a ruler are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch brought back a strange design.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond what is natural or normal, hence extraordinary or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: United achieved victory, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: achieved victory means came first, triumphed

explanation.surface: A football report: United won, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club; it means joined as a single whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined together become a single whole, so united can mean as one.

clue.text: Cleric, very holy within? The reverse — a venomous type!

indicators.note: The reverse says the whole construction is then turned back to front
within puts the holy word inside the cleric word

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric's title
pi is crossword shorthand for pious, very holy

explanation.surface: A clergyman seems saintly inside, but is really the opposite: a snake in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' makes REPIV, which 'The reverse' turns round. It also teases that the cleric is the opposite of holy.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder and its relatives are poisonous snakes, a venomous kind of creature.

clue.text: Strict believers making jokes about educated female

indicators.note: about says the jokes word goes around the woman's name

parts.note: puns are jokes on words
Rita, from the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: Severe religious people tell jokes about a woman with an education.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play about a working-class woman studying literature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Puritans were Protestants with rigid moral and religious standards.

clue.text: Risks with daughter and son full of wrath

indicators.note: full of says the two family letters hold the wrath word between them

parts.note: anger is wrath

explanation.surface: Family hazards: a daughter and son who are both furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts ANGER between D and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazards or perils are things that put you at risk, so risks is a synonym.

clue.text: Feeling tense in front of teacher being nasty

indicators.note: being nasty suggests something turned bad, so these letters are scrambled
front of means only the first letter of the word teacher is used

explanation.surface: A pupil feels anxious while standing before a teacher who is being unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being nasty' scrambles 'tense in' into SENTIEN, with the teacher's initial left unscrambled at the end; 'Feeling' looks like a verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is capable of sensation, so it is a feeling creature.

clue.text: Godly type goes round in leisurely walks

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a godly person
rolls means goes round, turns over and over

explanation.surface: A pious person takes gentle rambles in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried rambles taken for pleasure are strolls, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Initially sitting on child's toilet suffering from rash?

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits above the next
Initially means take only the opening letter of the word sitting

parts.note: a potty is a small toilet for a toddler

explanation.surface: A toddler perched on the potty has a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Having spots or pimples on the skin, as with a rash, is being covered in spots.

clue.text: Crime of minister wanting leader removed

indicators.note: wanting leader removed means the first letter of the minister word is dropped

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman's offence is that he wants his superior got rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Illustration from India engraved in copper

indicators.note: engraved in says the letter is cut into the other piece, placed inside it

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer, a PC or police constable
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian picture etched onto a copper plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal; it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal short form of picture, so a photograph or illustration.

clue.text: Fret when drippy folk are in the ascendant

indicators.note: in the ascendant means rising, so in a down answer the word is read upwards

parts.note: wets is British slang for feeble, ineffectual people

explanation.surface: Worry when weak, wishy-washy people are gaining power.
explanation.walkthrough: Wets was Thatcher's term for moderate Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew, or to stew, is informally to worry or be agitated.

clue.text: See some memories being conjured up

indicators.note: conjured up suggests raised upwards, so in a down answer the letters are read bottom to top
some means only part of the word memories is taken

explanation.surface: Look at a few recollections that are being brought to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the Holy See, the papal seat; 'conjured up' is not an anagram here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's jurisdiction, is based in this Italian capital city.

clue.text: Food dish absurdly presented to heathen idol

indicators.note: absurdly presented means set out in a ridiculous way, so the letters of to heathen idol are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal is offered, ridiculously, to a pagan statue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter.

clue.text: Spooner's appearance for what reason? Conceited fellow?

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: guise means outward appearance
why asks for what reason

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a smug man looks the way he does.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the sounds of GUISE and WHY gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec who thinks he knows it all is a cocky, self-satisfied man.

clue.text: Not all of the athletes in preliminary race

indicators.note: Not all of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only some of the runners take part in a qualifying round.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', but the answer is a noun and 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualifying round of a race, whose winners go on to the final, is a heat.
